newsitem.title: UK: ACPC 95/6 coffee exports below target, no new move.
newsitem.headline: ACPC 95/6 coffee exports below target, no new move.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) said on Saturday the group's exports in 1995/96 (July/June) reached 44.83 million 60-kg bags against a target of 45.8 million.

"There was a shortfall of 2.19 percent of the target and this is seen as positive by the member countries," ACPC president Rubens Antonio Barbosa of Brazil told reporters at the end of an ACPC council meeting in London.
ACPC members account for more than 80 percent of world's coffee production.
Preliminary ACPC figures issued on Monday showed exports from the group in 1995/96 reached 47 million bags. But the figures were later reviewed downward when a small group of producers met in Friday.
ACPC officials said the export data were based on figures prepared by producer-consumer group the International Coffee Organisation (ICO) July/June data released last month.
But the one-day meeting, as expected, made no major policy revisions and ACPC officials said the 14-member grouping would maintain its existing its existing export programme.
"The idea is just to continue with the second export programme," ACPC secretary-general Robeiro Oliviera Silva said. "There are no new proposals."
The ACPC last met in May when it agreed a new plan to limit green coffee exports from its members to 53.5 million bags in the year to June 1997.
The meeting made no review of the progress of its current export scheme, saying that it was still too early.
But Oliveiro said ACPC's export programme would be up for a review when its technical group comprising top growers meets in Costa Rica in November to study market situation.
The subsequent technical group meeting will be held in February either in Colombia or Indonesia.
At Saturday's meeting, Ecuador refuted ICO's export estimate of 645,000 bags for the country, saying that it was not line with its national estimate of 1.25 million bags.
Elsewhere, Barbosa said Zaire has formally joined the ACPC, bringing the total membership to 14.
Other key growers outside the ACPC include Vietnam, Mexico and Guatemala.
